lenses.lens: Unit economics & capital efficiency (COGS, labour intensity, throughput, capex, margins, break-even)

scores.rationale: Best item margins: beverage COGS is about 30% of the gross price at affordable-premium prices (C2 §3.4 recipe COGS at our prices). It has the smallest equipment package (C2 lean, USD 38–43k, less the AMD 3.32M Merrychef) and the fastest window. But the ticket is the lowest: 1.1 drinks × AMD 1,522 ≈ AMD 1,704 per order, which leaves only AMD 999 of contribution per order. Labour is a near-fixed cost (C3 lean roster, 3 per shift, 07–22, AMD 3.31M/month + meals/transport), so break-even is 149–170 tx/day against an evidence band of 80–150 (A2 §4.8; ≈110 in C6 §4). Capex is ≈AMD 134M ($370k) on a lean standalone M4 build. There is no lever to raise the ticket, and the concept competes head-on with Coffee House's AMD 1,000 drinks on the same corridor (A2 [S11]).

Food lifts contribution per order by 16% (AMD 1,160 vs 999) at a small cost: about +AMD 11M capex (20 m² prep area plus speed oven/griddle, C1/C2) and about +AMD 0.4M/month labour (a 6 h/day peak helper). A lavash breakfast wrap costs AMD 457 against a AMD 1,500 price, i.e. 30% COGS (A4 §3.11). Food mix COGS is 37%, so the blend stays at 31.5% + 2% waste. That is inside C6's 31–36% band. Bake-off and assembled food needs no hood and no cook, and keeps the window at ≤60 s. Break-even is still 141–159 tx/day, at the top of the evidence band. A mid-spec standalone M4 build (≈AMD 238M) never pays back at evidence volumes. This is the right menu, but it needs a cheaper real-estate model.

Contribution margin is only 45%. Meat items run ≈48% food cost: ESTIMATE by analogy with C2's full wrap at 47.6% of gross, and the shawarma price ceiling is AMD 1,150–1,350 (A4 [2][3]). Each cook position adds ≈AMD 1.07M/month (C3: 3.11 FTE × 327,733 × 1.045). The concept also needs +30 m² of kitchen plus hood and fire suppression, for capex ≈AMD 265M ($732k). Shawarma takes 2–4 min to assemble (A4), so window time rises to 90–100 s, or 36–45 cars/h (C6 §3.4), against summer-weekend peaks of 43–66 cars/h. Break-even is 211–238 tx/day, and a 3-year payback needs 440–470 tx/day. The market is also saturated, and fast food is eaten about once a week (A4 [34]).

scores.concept: (4) Hybrid roadside convenience (coffee + bakery + grab-and-go + restrooms + EV/fuel-station partnership)
scores.rationale: This scores 7 only in its capex-light form: co-located on a partner's fuel-station forecourt or interchange, with the partner owning the restrooms, EV charging and paving. C1 prices that site at ≈AMD 70.5M against 91.9M (lean) or 183.2M (mid) greenfield. It avoids the M4 access lanes (AMD 7–28M) and the substation risk (+10–30M). All-in capex is ≈AMD 110M ($304k), the best sales/capex of the four at 1.04 at 150 tx/day (prototype: 0.30). Break-even is 129–147 tx/day, also the best of the four, and captive traffic supports volume (WOG ≈117 cups/station/day, C6 [28]). Two conditions apply. Partner rent or revenue-share terms are unknown. EV and retail revenue must stay with the partner, because the catering turnover tax (TT) charges 20% of non-catering turnover (C4 Art. 258). The standalone version, with its own restrooms, EV and café (= the current prototype), scores about 2.

lenses.recommended_concept: Concept 2's menu in Concept 4's real-estate model. The menu is coffee plus a narrow set of hand-held Armenian breakfast and bakery items, bake-off or assembled, with no fryer, grill or cook. The unit sits on a partner fuel-station or interchange forecourt close to Yerevan/Abovyan. It is a single pickup window with tablet runners and a 10–13-car stack, in a 90–120 m² building. The partner owns the restrooms, EV charging and paving. Target all-in capex is ≤ AMD 110–150M ($0.30–0.41M), against ≈AMD 375M ($1.04M) for the current 171 m² dual-lane standalone prototype. Do not build the prototype as specified: at evidence volumes it needs 200–235 tx/day to break even and more than 500 tx/day for a 3-year payback.
key_arguments: Labour is quasi-fixed and dominates the P&L. A 3-per-shift, 07–22, 7-day roster costs AMD 3.31M/month (C3 §3.9, ads read as net), and the highway location adds meals, staff transport (0.3–0.6M) and recruitment. C2 therefore carries ≈AMD 4.33M/month of labour, which is 64% of sales at 110 tx/day. C6's 22–32% labour band is only reached at ≈220 tx/day. ESTIMATE: 4.33M × 12 / (220 × 2,050 × 360) ≈ 32%.

Ticket built from the menu mix (ESTIMATE). Average drink = C2's beverage mix at our prices = AMD 1,497, plus paid modifiers (10% of drinks × 250) = AMD 1,522; COGS 459 (30.2% of gross). Coffee + bakery ticket = 1.1 drinks × 1,522 + 35% attach × 1.1 items × AMD 975 = **AMD 2,050** (range 1,790–2,385). The model's AMD 2,600 ticket would need 1.25 drinks and ≈65% food attach, above A4's 30–45%. It should be cut.

Contribution per order decides the ranking: C1 AMD 999 (59%), C2 1,160 (57%), C4 1,177 (56%), C3 1,131 (45%). Variable costs are COGS + 1–2% waste (C6) + 1.4% card fees (C4/C2) + 3% marketing (C6) + 2% admin (C4) + 3.5–5% catering TT (C4 §3.5).

Break-even tx/day (base / lean roster): C1 170/149; C2 lean shell 159/141; C2 mid-spec 176/144; C3 238/211; C4 co-located 147/129; prototype 235/200. The evidence band is 80–150 (A2), with ≈110 base (C6). Every concept needs the top of the band or more just to break even.

Capex is the binding constraint. Under catering TT, which is the recommended regime (5–6.5% of receipts vs ≈10% VAT + profit tax, C4), the 20% VAT inside capex cannot be recovered, so every AMD of build costs 1.2. Site works are 31–37% of C1's budgets, and M4 access works (AMD 7–28M) and substation risk (+10–30M) apply only to greenfield highway pads.

The prototype is flagship-class. ESTIMATE: interpolating between C1 mid (183.2M) and flagship (376.3M) at the 171 m²/3,256 m² scale gives 332M; value-engineering takes it to ≈300M of construction. With equipment (≈52M), IT and launch, all-in is ≈AMD 375M ($1.04M). At 150 tx/day its sales/capex is 0.30, against Dutch Bros ≈1.2× (C1 §4).

Payback reality, even in the leanest case. Concept 4 co-located, with a demand-shaped roster and 07–19 trading (13 h on site), has fixed costs of ≈AMD 4.08M/month. That gives break-even at ≈116 tx/day, a 5-year payback at ≈172 tx/day and a 3-year payback at ≈208 tx/day, roughly 2× the C6 base of ≈110. Volume must be proven before capex is committed: field counts at the Coffee House M4 drive-thru (A2/C6) and a pop-up test (A4).

Food raises contribution and differentiates, but it must stay narrow. Bakery and assembled items run at 37% COGS, versus 30% for drinks. Hot meals run ≈48% and need a cook, a hood and 90–100 s windows. Coffee House sells sweets but no savoury food (A4 [7]). The lavash wrap (30% COGS) is the hero item; bought-in gata, lahmajo and khachapuri at 45–67% food cost are the weakest (A4 §3.11).

The throughput design should match Armenian volumes. At 150 tx/day the weekday AM peak is 21–33 cars/h, and summer weekends reach 43–66 cars/h (C6 §3.4). One window with runner tablets handles 60–80 cars/h (C6), so dual order lanes and a 2-lane digital board (AMD 14M vs 6.5M, C1) can be phased: C1 says phasing the flagship saves AMD 40–60M. Keep the cheap asphalt stack (10–13 cars).

Choose equipment for serviceability. The C2 lean or mid package (USD 38–43k or 77–88k) built on brands The Horeca services covers 250–600 drinks/day. The flagship Eversys + TurboChef package (USD 167–180k) has no local service and adds ≈AMD 45M of capex for throughput the unit will not need (C2 §3.1).
lenses.menu_architecture:
Target about 20 SKUs on the board, so the window stays at ≤60 s and food prep at ≤90 s (C6 §3.5; customisation causes 43% of US order errors).

(A) CORE BEVERAGES, about 82% of revenue. Espresso 900, Americano 350 ml 1,100, Cappuccino 300 ml 1,400, Latte 400 ml 1,600, Iced latte 450 ml 1,700, Cold-brew iced 1,600 (sold as 'smooth iced coffee', not black cold brew; A4), Signature flavoured hot or iced (apricot, sea-buckthorn; brand hero) 1,900, Hot chocolate 1,400, Batch lemonade 450 ml 1,200, Jezve-to-go 800 (local signature; the fast-brew device is unverified, A4), Herbal tea 700. Paid modifiers at +250: oat milk (+115 cost, A4), syrup and extra shot. Mix weights follow C2 §3.4: espresso 4 / americano 15 / cappuccino 13 / latte 18 / iced latte 16 / cold brew 6 / flavoured 16 / hot chocolate 5 / lemonade 7 (%).

(B) FOOD, about 18% of revenue. All items are hand-held and bake-off or assembled: no fryer, grill, rotisserie or hood, and no cook position. Mix and price (cost): lavash breakfast wrap with egg, cheese and herbs, basturma +300, 30% of food items, 1,500 (457); bake-off croissant 10%, 900 (370); croissant sandwich 10%, 1,400 (≈694); fresh-filled ponchik 20%, 400 (≈168); mini Gavar gata 15%, 600 (≈240); zhingyalov hats 10%, 900 (≈315; move in-house later); cheese pastry 5%, 700 (≈360). Food average AMD 975, COGS 37%. Frozen bake-off with weekly delivery plus a UHT milk buffer, per C2 §3.3.6.

(C) GRAB-AND-GO, 2–3 chilled SKUs: Jermuk/Bjni water and bottled tan at AMD 300–600. These are traffic items at ≈60% COGS, sold as part of the catering service so they stay under catering TT (C4 §3.5c).

(D) COMBOS: coffee + pastry 1,900–2,000; coffee + wrap 2,600 (A4 band 1,900–2,600).

(E) SEASONAL: rotate 3–4 SKUs (summer lemonades and iced; winter thyme tea and gata).

EXCLUDED: burgers, shawarma, hot meals (Concept 3 economics). Energy 'Rebels' are a limited test only (≈40–50% COGS, A4). Retail beans, mugs and merchandise must go through a separate VAT entity or be dropped, because catering TT taxes non-catering turnover at 20% (C4). EV charging must be the partner's revenue and capex.
lenses.pricing_notes:
TIER: affordable premium. Core drinks sit 40–70% above the mass leader and 13–28% below premium chains. Menu prices include tax and are identical under either regime.

PRICE POINTS (AMD) vs Coffee House (A2 [S11] Glovo, Oct 2026) and Coffeeshop Company (A2 [S12], VERIFIED):
- Americano 1,100 (vs 800 / 1,850)
- Cappuccino 300 ml 1,400 (vs 1,000 / 1,950)
- Latte 400 ml 1,600 (vs 1,000 / 1,950)
- Iced latte 450 ml 1,700 (vs 1,000 / 1,950)
- Signature 1,900
- Espresso 900; lemonade 1,200; jezve 800; modifiers +250

These sit within A2's affordable-premium band (cappuccino/latte 1,400–1,600, iced latte 1,600–1,800, signature 1,800–2,200).

COGS at these prices (C2 §3.4 recipes): cappuccino 29.7%, latte 31.0%, iced latte 26.0%, americano 24.3%, flavoured 37.0%, hot chocolate 43.9%. Beverage blend 30.2% of gross.

ATV FROM MENU MIX (ESTIMATE):
- Average drink 1,497 + modifiers 25 = 1,522.
- Concept 1 = 1.1 × 1,522 + 5% × 600 = **1,704**.
- Concept 2 = 1,674 + 35% × 1.1 × 975 = **2,050**.
- Concept 4 = 2,050 + 15% × 400 grab-and-go = **2,110**.
- Concept 3 = 0.9 × 1,100 + 70% × 1.2 × 1,800 = **2,502**.

The inputs of 1.1 drinks/order, 35% attach and 1.1 items per food order are ASSUMPTIONS. Basis: commuter-solo weekdays (C6/B1 AM peak), Sevan leisure groups at weekends, and A4's 30–45% attach range.

Concept 2 sensitivity: 1,790 (1.0 drink, 25% attach) to 2,385 (1.25 drinks, 45% attach).

Cross-checks:
- A4 base ticket 1,500–1,900 assumes one drink; our one-drink version is ≈1,897.
- Coffee Like car-pavilion check ≈1,672 AMD (A2 [S24]; REPORTED, Russia, franchisor 'from' claim, not labelled drive-through).
- The model's 2,600 is unsupported (it needs 1.25 drinks + 65% attach).

TIER TEST (C2 lean-shell, lean roster, fixed ≈4.93M/month):

| Tier | Avg drink (AMD) | Beverage COGS | ATV (AMD) | Contribution per order (AMD) | Break-even (tx/day) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mass (Coffee House-level: 800 / 1,000) | 1,003 | 45.8% | 1,404 | 591 | **278** |
| Affordable premium | 1,522 | 30.2% | 2,050 | 1,161 | **142** |
| Premium (C2 targets: latte 1,700, iced 2,000, flavoured 2,100) | 1,716 | 26.8% | 2,319 | 1,398 | **118** |

Premium beats affordable premium only if it loses less than 17% of volume. That is implausible:
- A2 puts a 1,950 cappuccino at 1.1 h of average gross pay.
- The incumbent drive-thru on the same road charges 800–1,200.
- A4 reports 38% of households have money 'enough only for food' or less.

C2 itself shows latte COGS rising from 35% to 41% of net under a 15% price cut. Harvest the premium only through large sizes and signature iced drinks at 1,900–2,200 for Sevan-weekend traffic.

TAX: catering turnover tax is the base case (C4). The VAT regime would cut contribution from ≈57% to ≈49% of receipts and raise break-even by about 16% (ESTIMATE).

Card fees: model 1.4% (C2 blended 1.35%). The CBA fee cap excludes MCC 5812/5814.
risks: Volume. Break-even is 129–176 tx/day for coffee-led formats. That sits at or above the top of the evidence band (A2 80–150, an ASSUMPTION; C6 ≈110). At 110 tx/day every configuration loses AMD 8–53M a year. Field counts at the Coffee House M4 drive-thru and a fuel-station pop-up are a gating item before any capex.

Capex overrun. C1 estimates carry ±25–35% accuracy. Substation risk adds +AMD 10–30M, rock excavation +3.5–5M and M4 access scope −7/+10M. Under TT all of these land at 1.2× because capex VAT cannot be recovered.

Labour inflation and ambiguity. Hospitality wages are rising 7–8% a year (C3; Armstat +7.8% y/y). Whether job-ad pay is net or gross swings payroll by ±27%. 2027 health-insurance rules add 2–3%. A dormant 35-hour-week draft is a +14% tail risk.

Price pressure from the incumbent. Coffee House sells at 800–1,200 on the same corridor (A2; the fact-check could not re-confirm the hot price range, iced is 900–1,000) and can fix its 20–40-minute waits cheaply. A forced 15% price cut raises latte COGS from 35% to 41% of net (C2).

Input cost and FX. The green coffee unit value rose 192% between 2019 and 2025, and coffee CPI was +9.5% in 2025 (A2, Comtrade/Armstat). 50–60% of beverage COGS is imported, and the AMD is strong at about 362/USD (C2). The wholesale coffee price (AMD 12,000/kg) is an ASSUMPTION without quotes.

Tax policy. Catering TT is a political concession whose headline rate was doubled in 2025. A forced move to VAT costs about 8 points of contribution (ESTIMATE), and C4 asks for a 'forced VAT from year 3' downside. Whether wages and rent are deductible under TT is unconfirmed: if they are not, TT rises by 1.5–2.5 points.

Partnership terms (concept 4). Fuel-station rent or revenue share, exclusivity and restroom/EV obligations are unknown. Max Oil already runs Max Cafe (coffee and hot dogs) at M4 km 12.2 (A4 [27]), so a partner may also be a competitor.

Non-catering income trap. EV charging, retail beans and merchandise booked inside the catering-TT company are taxed at 20% of turnover (C4 Art. 258). They need a separate VAT entity or must be left to the partner.

Food waste and supply on the M4. Fresh pastry keeps 1–3 days and milk needs 3–7 deliveries a week (C2 §3.3.6). Deductible waste is capped at 1–2% of income (C4). Summer/winter swings increase stock-out and waste. No Armenian importer of frozen viennoiserie has been identified.

Equipment uptime. Eversys, WMF, Schaerer, Merrychef and TurboChef have no Armenian service partner (C2). One breakdown during the summer peak could close the window for days. Specify brands with local service and a spares kit (5–8% of equipment value).
lenses.markdown:
# Unit economics & capital efficiency: concept screen (CHAMPA drive-thru)

*Lens: COGS, labour intensity, throughput, capex, margins, break-even. Prepared 2026-10-10. FX: CBA 361.93 AMD/USD.*

*Every figure comes from the research files (file id + section/source) or is labelled ESTIMATE (formula shown) or ASSUMPTION (basis given).*

## Verdict

**Ranking:** (4) capex-light hybrid **7.0**; (2) coffee + bakery **6.5**; (1) beverages only **4.5**; (3) broad fast food **2.0**.

**Recommendation:** Concept 2's menu (coffee + bake-off/assembled Armenian hand-helds) in Concept 4's real-estate model: a partner fuel-station or interchange forecourt near Yerevan/Abovyan. Use one pickup window with tablet runners and a 90–120 m² building. The partner owns the restrooms, EV charging and paving.

**Tier:** affordable premium. Coffee + bakery ATV is about AMD 2,050.

**The current prototype should not be built as specified.** It is 171 m², with a café, restrooms, dual lanes, 2 windows and its own M4 accel/decel lanes. All-in it costs about AMD 375M ($1.04M) excluding land. It needs 200–235 tx/day to break even and more than 500 tx/day for a 3-year payback.

## 1. Price tier and ATV (built from the menu mix)

### Beverage price points (VAT/TT-inclusive)

COGS are from the C2 §3.4 recipes (ESTIMATE built on SAS [S40] and Oval Pack [S43] prices).

| Item | Price (AMD) | COGS (AMD) | COGS % | Coffee House (A2 [S11]) | Coffeeshop Co (A2 [S12]) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Espresso | 900 | 132 | 14.7% | – | – |
| Americano 350 ml | 1,100 | 267 | 24.3% | 800 | 1,850 |
| Cappuccino 300 ml | 1,400 | 416 | 29.7% | 1,000 | 1,950 |
| Latte 400 ml | 1,600 | 496 | 31.0% | 1,000 | 1,950 |
| Iced latte 450 ml | 1,700 | 442 | 26.0% | 1,000 | 1,950 |
| Cold-brew iced 450 ml | 1,600 | 325 | 20.3% | – | – |
| Signature flavoured 400 ml | 1,900 | 703 | 37.0% | – | – |
| Hot chocolate | 1,400 | 614 | 43.9% | – | – |
| Lemonade 450 ml | 1,200 | 391 | 32.6% | – | – |

- **Weighted at C2's mix:** average drink AMD 1,497. With paid modifiers (10% × 250) it is **AMD 1,522**, with COGS 459 (**30.2%** of gross).
- **Food (A4 §3.11 / C2 §3.4 costs; mix is an ASSUMPTION):**
  - wrap 1,500 (457)
  - croissant 900 (370)
  - croissant sandwich 1,400 (≈694)
  - ponchik 400 (≈168)
  - mini gata 600 (≈240)
  - zhingyalov 900 (≈315)
  - cheese pastry 700 (≈360)

  Food average **AMD 975, COGS 37.2%**.

### ATV by concept (ESTIMATE)

| Concept | Drinks | Food | Other | **ATV** | COGS % (gross) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Beverages only | 1.1 × 1,522 | 5% × 600 | – | **1,704** | 30.5% |
| 2 Coffee + bakery | 1.1 × 1,522 | 35% × 1.1 × 975 | – | **2,050** | 31.5% |
| 3 Broad fast food | 0.9 × 1,100 | 70% × 1.2 × 1,800 | – | **2,502** | 42.9% |
| 4 Hybrid | as 2 | as 2 | 15% × 400 grab-and-go | **2,110** | 32.3% |

- **Basis for the inputs (ASSUMPTION):** 1.1 drinks/order, 35% attach and 1.1 items per food order. Weekdays are mostly solo commuters; weekends bring leisure groups; A4 gives 30–45% attach.
- **Concept 2 range:** 1,790 to 2,385.
- **Cross-checks:**
  - A4's one-drink ticket of 1,540–1,860; our one-drink version is 1,897.
  - Coffee Like car-pavilion check of about 1,672 AMD (A2 [S24]; REPORTED franchisor claim, not labelled drive-through).
- **The model's AMD 2,600 ticket needs 1.25 drinks and about 65% food attach. It should be cut.**

### Tier test (fixed costs AMD 4.93M/month)

| Tier | ATV (AMD) | Contribution per order (AMD) | Break-even (tx/day) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mass (Coffee House prices) | 1,404 | 591 | **278** |
| **Affordable premium** | **2,050** | **1,161** | **142** |
| Premium (C2 targets) | 2,319 | 1,398 | 118 |

Premium wins only if it loses less than 17% of volume. A2's affordability evidence and the incumbent's AMD 800–1,200 pricing make that unlikely.

## 2. Cost structure (catering turnover-tax regime, C4)

### Variable costs (% of gross receipts)

| Item | Rate | Source |
|---|---|---|
| COGS | 30.5–42.9% | §1 |
| Waste | 1–2% | C6 |
| Card fees | 1.4% | C4 model; C2 1.35% |
| Marketing | 3% | C6 |
| Admin | 2% | C4 |
| Turnover tax | 3.5% floor at break-even; ≈4.2–5% at 200 tx/day | C4 formula: 12% − 9% × e |

Contribution margin per order:

| Concept | AMD per order | Margin |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | 999 | 59% |
| C2 | 1,160 | 57% |
| C4 | 1,177 | 56% |
| C3 | 1,131 | 45% |

### Fixed costs (AMD M/month, base roster / lean roster)

Inputs:
- **Labour (C3 §3.9):** lean roster 3.31M; plus meals at 15k/FTE, staff transport 0.3–0.6M and recruitment 41–88k.
  - C2 adds a 6 h/day peak helper.
  - C3 adds a cook position of about +1.07M.
  - The lean variant is demand-shaped: −21% paid hours.
- **Utilities, ESTIMATE:** 10–15 kW × 17 h × 30.4 days × ≈51 AMD/kWh (C1 tariff), plus water and telecom, gives 0.45–0.70M.
- **Ground lease:** 0.5M (C4 model, AMD 6M a year).
- **Equipment service:** 4% a year of equipment value (C2: 3–5%).
- **Property and local taxes:** ≈0.05–0.15M (C4).

| Configuration | Fixed (base / lean) |

| C1 | 5.11 / 4.47 |
| C2, lean shell | 5.54 / 4.93 |
| C2, mid spec | 6.13 / 5.01 |
| C3 | 8.07 / 7.17 |
| C4, co-located | 5.18 / 4.57 |
| Prototype | 8.30 / 7.05 |

**Labour intensity:** C2 labour is 64% of sales at 110 tx/day. C6's 22–32% band needs about 220 tx/day.

## 3. Capex (incl. VAT, which a TT payer cannot recover)

All configurations below include IT (AMD 3M, C4), launch (AMD 12M, the model's figure via C6) and one month of pre-opening payroll. Equipment includes +16.5% for installation and spares (C2).

| Configuration | Build-up | AMD M | USD |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1, lean standalone M4 | C1 lean 91.9 + access upgraded to mid spec 10.8 + equipment 13 (C2 lean without speed oven) | 134 | $370k |
| C2, lean shell M4 | C1 lean 91.9 + access 10.8 + 20 m² prep 5.6 + equipment 18 | 145 | $401k |
| C2, mid spec | C1 mid 183.2 + equipment 35 (C2 mid) | 238 | $658k |
| C3 | C1 mid 183.2 + 30 m² kitchen 9 + hood 5 (ASSUMPTION) + equipment 49 (incl. hot line, ASSUMPTION) | 265 | $732k |
| C4, fuel-station co-located | C1 co-location 70.5 + equipment 21 | 110 | $304k |
| **Prototype** | Interpolated between C1 mid and flagship: 183.2 + 0.77 × (376.3 − 183.2) = 332, value-engineered to ≈300; + equipment ≈52 + launch/IT/pre-opening | **≈375 (range 340–420)** | **$1.04M** |

The prototype carries about AMD 62M of VAT that cannot be recovered.

## 4. Break-even and payback (ESTIMATE; 360 trading days)

| Configuration | Break-even tx/day (base / lean) | EBITDA @110 tx/day, lean (AMD M/yr) | EBITDA @150 tx/day, lean (AMD M/yr) | tx/day for 5-yr / 3-yr payback (lean) | Sales/capex @150 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | 170 / 149 | −14.1 | +0.3 | 230 / 281 | 0.69 |
| C2, lean shell | 159 / 141 | −13.2 | +3.6 | 217 / 264 | 0.76 |
| C2, mid spec | 176 / 144 | −14.2 | +2.5 | 265 / 343 | 0.47 |
| C3 | 238 / 211 | −41.2 | −24.9 | 353 / 443 | 0.51 |
| **C4, co-located** | **147 / 129** | **−8.2** | **+8.7** | **186 / 222** | **1.04** |
| Prototype | 235 / 200 | −38.0 | −21.0 | 387 / 508 | 0.30 |

**Best case.** C4 with a lean roster and 07:00–19:00 trading (13 h on site) has fixed costs of about AMD 4.08M/month. That gives:
- break-even at about 116 tx/day;
- 5-year payback at about 172 tx/day;
- 3-year payback at about 208 tx/day.

**Evidence band:** 80–150 tx/day (A2), with about 110 in C6, WOG's captive fuel stations at about 117 cups/day, and Coffee Like's car pavilions at about 103 checks/day.

**Volume must be proven before any capex is committed.**

## 5. Design implications

1. Shrink the building to 90–120 m² (C6). Drop or minimise the café seating.
2. Restrooms and EV charging belong to the partner.
3. Use one pickup window plus runner tablets, which handle 60–80 cars/h (C6). Phase the second order lane and the 2-lane digital board: AMD 14M vs 6.5M, and C1 says phasing saves 40–60M.
4. Keep the 10–13-car stack.
5. Equip with the C2 lean or mid package from brands with local service (The Horeca). Do not use Eversys or TurboChef.

## 6. Key risks

- **Volume:** break-even sits at or above the top of the evidence band.
- **Capex:** ±25–35%, plus substation risk.
- **Labour:** wages +7–8% a year, and ±27% depending on whether ads are net or gross.
- **Incumbent:** Coffee House can respond on price and speed.
- **Coffee cost and FX.**
- **Turnover-tax policy:** a forced move to VAT costs about 8 points of contribution.
- **Partner terms:** unknown.
- **20% tax on non-catering income** if EV or retail revenue sits in the catering company.
- **M4 waste and logistics.**
- **Equipment service:** no local partner for the flagship brands.

lenses.lens: Armenian customer & market fit: purchasing power, habits, segments, willingness to pay, drive-thru culture and seasonality. Sources: A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and B3, all read in full. Where a file's fact-check corrected a value, the corrected value is used. FX is CBA 361.93 AMD/USD (9 Oct 2026).

scores.rationale:
Weakest fit, scoring 3.6 on the weighted matrix. Criterion scores: affordability 4, habit 3, differentiation 2, segment coverage 2, seasonality 6, ops 6.

- Specialty coffee is a small, sit-down niche in central Yerevan (Kentron). wte.am lists 22 venues, which the fact-check reduced to about 16 brands. Micro-lot origin imports were only about 54 t in 2025. A2 §3.3 says "Nothing we found indicates it travels to highways".
- Robusta-origin beans are 89% of green coffee imports, consistent with jezve brewing (A2 [S2]). Espresso-type coffee is about 10–15% of national volume (A2, ASSUMPTION).
- On the M4, a drinks-only menu meets Coffee House Drive-Thru head-on. Its cappuccino costs 800–1,200 AMD (A2 [S10]; the fact-check re-saw only the iced range of 700–1,000) and its iced drinks 700–1,000. Max Cafe operates on both carriageways at km 12.2 (A3 [24]).
- The ticket is capped at about 1,300–1,500 AMD (A2 §4.2). The only drive-format benchmark, Coffee Like's Russian car pavilion, has a check of ≈1,672 AMD (A2 [S24]). That figure is a franchisor "from" claim, and the page does not say "drive-through".
- It does not serve the families, long-distance drivers and truckers who want food and restrooms (B3 §3.8).
- Across the region, drive lanes belong to fast-food chains, not coffee shops: Poland has 459 tagged drive-thrus, of which about 3 are coffee (A5 [32]).
- Its only strengths are drink margins and a simple operation.

Best customer-product fit, scoring 7.4. Criterion scores: affordability 8, habit 7, differentiation 7, segment coverage 7, seasonality 7, ops 8.

- **Armenians eat dough first.** Bread and flour supply 53% of adult energy. Pastry is the most-consumed fast food in Yerevan at 76 g/day, ahead of fried chicken at 53 g and burgers/hot dogs at 50 g (A4 [35][34]).
- **This is the documented white space.** No operator combines barista coffee with hot savoury hand-helds. Coffee House sells sweets only, fuel stations sell hot dogs, and fast-food chains list no hot coffee (A3 §1.8; A4 §3.8).
- **The breakfast slot is open.** 13 of 14 KFC units open at 10:00 (A3 §3.1).
- **The core items suit a car.**
  - A4's suitability scores: gata 26/30, lavash breakfast wrap 24, ponchik 23.
  - Reheat or assembly takes 90 s or less.
  - Item prices of 400–1,600 AMD sit inside local anchors.
  - An in-house lavash wrap runs at 29–39% food cost (A4 §3.11).
- **The commuter base is steady.** Segment A (Yerevan edge to Charentsavan) has only 1.5× peak/trough seasonality (B3 §3.7).
- **Penalties:**
  - There is no habit of buying breakfast out: Glovo's "Breakfast" filter returns 1 store of 33 (A4 [33]), so ramp-up will be slow.
  - Bought-in pastries run at 45–67% food cost.
  - Incumbents could copy the idea with a pie warmer within months (A4 §3.8; A3 §3.7).

scores.concept: (3) Broad fast-food & beverage menu (burgers/shawarma/hot meals + coffee)
scores.rationale:
Poor fit, scoring 4.6. Criterion scores: affordability 5, habit 5, differentiation 3, segment coverage 6, seasonality 5, ops 3.

**What supports it:**
- Regional drive-thrus are fast-food led: 20 of Georgia's 21 tagged drive-thrus are burger/sandwich chains (A5 [32]).
- Meals lift the ticket for families.

**What counts against it:**
- **The category is saturated and cheap** (A3 §3.2; A4 [14]):
  - KFC: 14 units, combos 2,800–3,200 AMD.
  - Tashir: 29 points, burger 1,300–1,350 AMD.
  - Mr. Gyros: 17 branches.
  - Karas: 10 branches.
  - 12 shawarma outlets on Glovo.
  - A mainstream fast-food meal costs 1,700–3,200 AMD.
- **A4 rejects the core items.** It rates shawarma 17/30 ("No") and hot dogs 20/30 ("No", a fuel-station commodity), and says burgers are "not core".
- **Fast food is eaten only about once a week** (A4 [34]).
- **Wendy's is the real American burger drive-thru threat.** It opened in Dec 2025 with 20 units planned by 2030 (A3 [11][12]).
- **Complex hot production causes exactly the incumbent's problem.** Coffee House Drive-Thru reviews report 20–60-minute waits, and its written reviews average 3.76★ (A3 [22]).
- **Analogs:**
  - McDonald's Bolivia exited over "poor sales and high prices".
  - McDonald's Kazakhstan exited when imported patties were blocked (A5 [14]).
- **It does little for the weekday breakfast commuter**, who is the year-round base.

scores.concept: (4) Hybrid roadside convenience (coffee + bakery + grab-and-go + restrooms + EV/fuel-station partnership)
scores.rationale:
Best format coverage but diluted, scoring 6.8. Criterion scores: affordability 7, habit 7, differentiation 5, segment coverage 9, seasonality 7, ops 5.

**What supports it:**
- **Roadside coffee scaled on fuel forecourts in the region.**
  - Ukraine: WOG sold more than 70,000 cups/day across 386 cafés, ≈181 cups per point per day (A5 [19]).
  - Georgia: 27 of 72 Dunkin' outlets sit within 60 m of a fuel station (A5 [32]).
- **Restrooms and seats serve high-ticket groups.** Families, leisure trippers and long-distance travellers are the big-basket orders (B3 §3.8).
- **Georgia-linked traffic and trucks are better captured by a fuel-station hybrid.** B3 puts Georgia-linked traffic at 1,200–2,100 vehicles/day on Sevan–Dilijan, including about 400–700 trucks (B3 §3.6, §4.6).
- **Walk-up is mandatory.** Only 41.2–46% of households own a car (A1 [9]; A5 [8]).
- **A5 rates the format higher than a standalone highway unit:** 45–55% odds for a fuel hybrid against 25–35% for a standalone M4 pad.

**What counts against it:**
- **Forecourt cafés are already being rolled out:**
  - Max Oil: Max Cafe at 10 tagged stations, 11 including the km 12.2 left-side unit (fact-check corrected).
  - Flash: Express Cafe "opening soon".
  - Shell: Shell Café.
- **General grab-and-go retail duplicates what is already there.** Within 200 m of the M4 there are 60 fuel stations and 26 convenience shops (A3).
- **EV demand is not evidenced.** The six files carry no data on the EV fleet.
- **The partner holds the leverage.**
- **Record fuel prices** (AI-95 at AMD 630/l) weigh on leisure trips (A1 [31]).

**Conclusion:** keep its restroom, walk-up and truck-bay elements, and drop broad retail.

lenses.recommended_concept:
Concept 2 is the customer proposition: specialty-grade but mainstream coffee plus localised Armenian breakfast and bakery hand-helds. It should be delivered in a "hybrid-lite" format that takes only the elements of Concept 4 that customers have proven they use:
- the drive lane plus a walk-up window and the 12 seats;
- the 2 restrooms, for families and long-distance travellers;
- a walk-up long-vehicle bay for truckers;
- packaged water and tan as add-ons.

What it should not include:
- No broad fast-food line.
- No general convenience retail.
- EV charging only as an amenity, not as a demand driver.

Co-location with or next to a fuel partner (CPS, which shows no food format online, or an independent CNG station) is preferred over a standalone pad.

"American-style" should describe the service standard (speed, app pre-order, consistency, clean restrooms), not the menu or the brand identity. The local CHAMPA brand is supported by the evidence (A4 §4.9; A5 §4.8).
lenses.positioning_tier:
**Affordable premium, with a mass-market entry tier.**

**Core prices (AMD, VAT included):**
- Cappuccino or latte, M 350 ml: 1,400 (≈$3.87).
- Iced latte, 450 ml: 1,600.
- Americano, 350 ml: 1,000.

**Entry tier (≤1,100 AMD):**
- Jezve-to-go: 800.
- Small 250 ml latte: 1,100.
- Ponchik: 400.
- Herbal tea: 600.

**Why not premium.** A Starbucks-level base of 2,000+ AMD is ruled out by local incomes:
- A 2,000-AMD drink feels like ≈$14 in PPP terms (A1 §3.7).
- Food away from home is only 2,293 AMD per month per urban resident (A1 [9]).
- 38% of households say money is enough only for food, or not even that (A4 [29]).

**Why not mass-market.** Matching 800–1,000 AMD fights Coffee House's 52-branch scale and Max Cafe, and cannot pay for the tuff/hypar building or carry the seasonal trough.

**Average transaction value (ATV):** **2,400 AMD per order including VAT**, which is ≈2,000 ex-VAT and ≈$6.63. It is built from about 2.2 items per order and 49% food attach. The range runs from about 2,200 (winter months) to 2,650 (summer months).
key_arguments:
**The local price ceiling is low; price is the binding constraint, not the drive-thru culture.**
- Mass to-go coffee is 800–1,000 AMD at Coffee House (Glovo, A2 [S11]).
- Numbeo's average cappuccino is 1,342 AMD (A2 [S13]).
- The premium chains stop at 1,800–1,950 AMD (Surf, Coffeeshop Company; A2 [S12][S20]).
- At 1,400 AMD, CHAMPA's medium latte is +40% vs Coffee House, ≈Numbeo's average and −28% vs Coffeeshop Company. It costs 0.77 h of average gross pay (1,400 ÷ 1,813 AMD/h, A2 basis).

**Habitual premium coffee buying is limited to the top income groups** (A1 §3.7, ESTIMATE on ILCS 2024 decile incomes).
- Eight 2,000-AMD drinks a month take ≥11.6% of per-capita income for deciles I–IX, so a weekly habit is realistic only for the top quintile (≈620k people).
- ESTIMATE (this lens): a commuter visiting 1.5×/week at a 1,745-AMD solo order spends ≈11.3k AMD/month. That is 4.6% of decile X and 8.2% of decile IX per-capita income.
- So model repeat frequency at ≤1.5 visits/week, plus a cheap entry tier.

**The menu must be dough-led and Armenian, not American.**
- Bread and flour supply 53% of energy, and 40% of adults eat pastry daily (A4 [35]).
- Pastry is the #1 fast food in Yerevan at 76 g/day (A4 [34]).
- A US donut at 800–1,000 AMD would cost 5–7× a 130–150 AMD Grand Candy ponchik (A4 [15]).
- There is no bagel culture.
- The US breakfast sandwich should be reformulated into a lavash wrap (A4 §3.10).

**The coffee + hot-savoury white space is real but time-limited.**
- Coffee House sells only sweets.
- Fast-food chains list no hot coffee.
- Fuel stations sell hot dogs.
- KFC opens at 10:00, leaving breakfast open (A3 §1.8, §3.1; A4 §3.8).
- The in-house lavash wrap runs at 29–39% food cost, against 45–67% for bought-in pastries (A4 §3.11).

**The drive-thru format is accepted, but throughput is the local failure mode.**
- Coffee House Drive-Thru has 4.9★ from 123 ratings and daily regulars.
- But its 17 written reviews average 3.76★, and 4 of the 5 written in Jun–Sep 2026 are 1–2★ for 20–60-minute waits and wrong orders (A3 [22]).
- So CHAMPA has to win on speed and accuracy, not on novelty: "first drive-thru on the M4" is factually unavailable (A2 §1.1, A3 §4.1).

**Car access caps a lane-only model, so walk-up, seats and restrooms are core.**
- 41.2% of households own a car (ILCS 2024), 42% in Yerevan (CB 2024) (A1 [9]; A5 [8]).
- Yerevan has the lowest Numbeo traffic index of the comparators (104), which weakens the drive-thru's time-saving pitch (A5 [1]).

**Commuters are the base, and tourism is only an upside layer** (B3).
- Weekday commuter car trips: ≈3.3–8.3k per direction.
- Short-stay sightseeing tourists: only ≈16% of 2.26m (≈0.37m).
- Gegharkunik takes 1.2% of national accommodation & food turnover.
- Seasonality: Segment A (Yerevan edge–Charentsavan) has a 1.5× peak/trough with 29% of traffic in Jun–Aug. Segment B (Hrazdan–Sevan) has 2.3×, with Jan at 69 and Aug at 151.

**ATV is built from the menu mix, not from US benchmarks.**
- Average handcrafted drink ≈1,320 AMD; average food item ≈970 AMD.
- Order types: solo commuter/regional 60% of orders at 1,745 AMD; group/family leisure 25% at 4,748; professional drivers 15% at 1,470.
- Combined: 2,455 gross, less ≈45 of combo discounts, ≈2,400 AMD.
- That is 69% of the average CBA card ticket of 3,473 AMD (A1 [21]). The solo order (1,745) is in line with A4's 1,540–1,860 and Coffee Like's 1,672-AMD drive check.

**The American identity is a liability.**
- Starbucks-Alshaya held talks in Armenia in Oct 2025 and launched in Tbilisi in Jul 2026 (A2 [S5][S7], REPORTED).
- Wendy's plans 20 units by 2030 (A3 [12]).
- Starbucks ready-to-drink coffee is already on SAS shelves at 1,250 AMD (A4 [23]).
- Imported concepts that did not localise failed: Starbucks in Israel and Australia, Dunkin' in Poland (A5 [24][25]).
- So the local CHAMPA brand is the right call.

**Choose the side of the road for the customer.**
- Right-in/right-out access serves only one carriageway.
- Commuter morning coffee happens on the Yerevan-bound side; leisure morning departures on the Sevan-bound side (B3 §4.4).
- Coffee House Drive-Thru sits on the Sevan-bound side at km 12.8 (A3).
- A Yerevan-bound site, beyond the km 10–13 cluster, captures weekday morning commuters plus weekend evening leisure returns, which are food-led and suit the savoury hand-helds. It also avoids a head-on fight with the incumbent (ASSUMPTION; for the site team to test).
lenses.menu_architecture:
**Overall shape:** about 28–32 SKUs at launch on 2 production lines: an espresso/iced bar, and a hot hand-held station with a griddle press and a high-speed oven. Every food item should take 90 s or less to prepare (A4 §3.9).

**A. Handcrafted drinks (10 SKUs, 3 sizes for milk espresso):**
- Jezve-to-go Armenian coffee (signature and entry item).
- Americano.
- Cappuccino/latte (S/M/L).
- Flat white.
- Iced latte.
- 2 signature sweet iced drinks (e.g. apricot-honey latte, salted-caramel iced).
- Batch lemonades (sea buckthorn, tarragon, apricot).
- Herbal tea (thyme, mint).
- Hot chocolate.
- Modifiers: oat or lactose-free milk, extra shot, syrup.

**B. Hot hand-helds (5–6 SKUs, the hero line):**
- Armenian breakfast lavash wrap (egg, cheese, herbs; basturma option), made in-house.
- Croissant sandwich (ham-cheese or chicken).
- Zhingyalov hats (vegetarian, year-round).
- Folded lahmajo with greens.
- Cheese puff pastry / Imeruli piece.
- Optional karkandak as a cheap anchor.

**C. Sweet bakery (4 SKUs, bought in from local suppliers):**
- Ponchik, filled to order (vanilla, apricot, matsun cream).
- Mini Gavar/Sevan gata.
- Cookie.
- Muffin.

**D. Packaged add-ons (4–6 SKUs):**
- Jermuk/Bjni water.
- Bottled tan.
- Kids' juice.
- Gata/ponchik gift box for the return trip and New Year.

**E. Combos (about 10% off à la carte):**
- Morning Wrap: medium latte + wrap.
- Road Snack: latte or iced latte + gata or ponchik.
- Family Road Box: 4 hand-helds + 4 drinks.

**Dayparts:**
- 07:00–11:00: commuter breakfast (wrap + coffee).
- 11:00–17:00: travel and leisure (hats, lahmajo, croissant sandwich, iced drinks, lemonade).
- 17:00–23:00: return trips (savoury food, tea, gift boxes).

**Seasonal rotation (3–4 SKUs):**
- Summer: lemonades and iced drinks become core.
- Winter: herbal tea, a punch and hot chocolate become core.

**Limited tests only:**
- 2 energy \"Rebel\" drinks, including a sugar-free one. A can of Red Bull retails at 670 AMD, and a Rebel would run at ≈50% food cost (A4).
- 1 US-style donut.
- Iced drinks made on a cold-brew base.

**Dropped from the US template:** bagels, English-muffin sandwiches, burgers, shawarma, hot dogs, Adjarian khachapuri (not car-friendly), fresh-squeezed juice and fish (A4 §3.9–3.10).

**Result:**

**Model and operating notes:**
- Card fee: use 1.5–2%. The 0.5–0.9% cap is unlikely to apply above AMD 150 m annual turnover (A1 fact-check).
- Index prices at about 4–5% a year: catering CPI is +4.6% and fast food +4.8% (A1 [7]). Coffee input costs are rising faster (retail coffee +14.7% in 2025).
- Do not anchor any core drink above 2,000 AMD.
risks:
**Willingness to pay is untested.** No Armenian survey measures it (A1 §5, A5 §5).
- The medium latte at 1,400 AMD is +40% vs Coffee House.
- 49.6% of households perceive "high" price growth (CBA Q3 2026; A1 [22]).
- Mitigation: run a Van Westendorp price survey (n≥600, Yerevan + Kotayk) and a 2-week pop-up price test before fixing the menu board.

**The breakfast-out habit is unproven.** Glovo's "Breakfast" filter returns 1 store of 33, and breakfast is a home meal that is often skipped (A4 §3.1).
- The hero wrap may ramp slowly.
- Mitigation: sell hand-helds all day and do not size the kitchen for breakfast alone.
**The menu is easy to copy.** Coffee House (52 branches, app pre-order already working) or Max Oil/Flash could add hot savoury items or fix their throughput within months (A3 §3.7; A4 §3.8).

**Seasonality and weather.**
- Segment B swings 2.3× and segment C 2.6× (B3 §3.7).
- ATV swings from ≈1,950 to ≈3,000.
- Sevan January mean is −6.1 °C, with ~32 snowfall days a year (B3 [14]).
- A site beyond Hrazdan would depend on 10–14 summer weekends, the same pattern as McDonald's seasonal Montenegro unit, which closed (A5 [14]).

**Tourism and relocant volatility.**
- Russia supplies 41% of tourists, and Russian tourist arrivals grew fastest (+23% in H1 2026).
- Armenia–Russia relations worsened in 2026 (A1 §3.13; B3 §4.7).
- Meghri (Iran) road crossings are down 32%.
- Base cases must not rely on these groups.

**Throughput.** Group and family orders of 4.3 items slow the lane, and the incumbent already fails at peak with 20–60-minute waits (A3 [22]).
- Design the hot line for 90 s or less per item, add pre-order, and cap the menu at about 30 SKUs.

**Input-cost inflation squeezes the affordable-premium margin.**
- Green coffee unit value is +192% since 2019, and coffee CPI rose 9.5% in 2025 (A2 [S2][S14]).
- Food CPI is 6.2% (A1 [8]).
- Hospitality wages are +7.8% y/y (A1 fact-check).
- Bought-in pastries run at 45–67% food cost (A4 §3.11).
**Starbucks (via Alshaya) or Wendy's drive lanes could out-American an American-style promise** (A2 [S5][S7]; A3 [12]). Keep the brand local.

**The behavioural evidence is thin.**
- Attach rates and group share are ASSUMPTIONS.
- The diet data come from a 2019 Yerevan survey of n=423 with a 90% university-educated sample, and from a 24-hour recall that does not state its fieldwork year (A4 §4.10).
- Mitigation: intercept surveys and receipt sampling at Coffee House Drive-Thru and Max Cafe km 12.2.

**Concept 4 add-ons carry unvalidated demand and possible tax drag.**
- No EV fleet data appear in A1–A5 or B3.
- A grep shows that C4-tax (not reviewed for this lens) says non-catering revenue such as EV charging is taxed at 20% of turnover under the catering declaration. That could also affect packaged retail. Finance should confirm.
**Record fuel prices could dampen leisure driving.** AI-95 is at AMD 630/l, petrol +11.7% y/y and diesel +25% (A1 [31][7]).
lenses.markdown:
# CHAMPA drive-thru: Armenian customer & market fit (lens report)

*Date: 2026-10-10. FX: CBA 361.93 AMD/USD (9 Oct 2026).*

*Evidence: A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and B3, all read in full. Where a file's fact-check (section 7) corrected a value, the corrected value is used. Each tag refers to the original source as cited in the file: VERIFIED, REPORTED, ESTIMATE (formula shown) or ASSUMPTION (basis given). No US benchmarks are used to calibrate Armenian values.*

---

## 1. Verdict

1. **The constraint is price, not drive-thru culture.**
   - Armenians already accept the format. The only local drive-thru, Coffee House on the M4, has 4.9★ from 123 ratings and daily regulars (A3 [22]).
   - The market, however, clears coffee at 800–1,000 AMD (A2 [S11]).
   - Food away from home averages only 2,293 AMD per urban resident per month (A1 [9], ILCS 2024).
2. **The best concept is Concept 2, coffee plus localised Armenian breakfast and bakery hand-helds (7.4/10).** It should run in a "hybrid-lite" format that keeps only the customer-proven parts of Concept 4 (6.8/10): restrooms, walk-up window and seats, a truck walk-up bay and packaged water/tan.
   - Specialty-only (3.6) is weak.
   - Broad fast-food (4.6) is weak.
3. **Positioning is affordable premium with a mass-market entry tier.**
   - Medium (350 ml) latte 1,400 AMD; iced latte (450 ml) 1,600 AMD; americano 1,000 AMD.
   - Entry tier: jezve 800, small latte 1,100, ponchik 400.
   - Do not anchor any core drink above 2,000 AMD.
4. **Base average transaction value (ATV) is about 2,400 AMD per order including VAT** (≈2,000 ex-VAT, ≈$6.63).
   - It is built from about 2.2 items per order and a 49% food attach rate.
   - Range: ≈2,200 in winter months to ≈2,650 in summer months; stress range ≈1,950–3,000.
5. **"American-style" should mean the service standard, not the menu or the identity.**
   - That service standard is speed, pre-order, consistency and clean restrooms.
   - The local CHAMPA brand is the right call.

---

## 2. Customer reality check

| Topic | Evidence | Source / status |

## 4. Concept scoring (0–10, weighted; ASSUMPTION scores built on cited evidence)

| Criterion (weight) | 1 Specialty beverages only | 2 Coffee + breakfast/bakery | 3 Broad fast-food | 4 Hybrid roadside convenience |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Affordability & ticket fit (20%) | 4 | 8 | 5 | 7 |
| Habit / diet fit (20%) | 3 | 7 | 5 | 7 |
| Differentiation vs incumbents (15%) | 2 | 7 | 3 | 5 |
| Corridor segment coverage (20%) | 2 | 7 | 6 | 9 |
| Seasonality resilience (10%) | 6 | 7 | 5 | 7 |
| Drive-thru speed / ops fit (15%) | 6 | 8 | 3 | 5 |
| **Weighted score** | **3.6** | **7.4** | **4.6** | **6.8** |

**Concept 1, specialty beverages only (3.6).**
- **Specialty coffee does not travel outside central Yerevan.** "Nothing we found indicates it travels to highways" (A2 §3.3). Micro-lot origin imports were about 54 t in 2025.
- **It meets the incumbents head-on at half its price.** Coffee House Drive-Thru charges 800–1,200 for a cappuccino and 700–1,000 for iced drinks, and Max Cafe runs on both carriageways at km 12.2 (A2/A3).
- **The ticket is capped at about 1,300–1,500 AMD** (A2 §4.2).
- **Coffee-only is rare in drive formats regionally.** Of Poland's 459 tagged drive-thrus, only about 3 are coffee (A5).

**Concept 2, coffee + breakfast/bakery (7.4).**
- **It matches how Armenians eat.** Bread and flour supply 53% of energy, and pastry is the #1 fast food (A4).
- **It fills the documented white space.** No operator combines coffee with hot savoury food; KFC opens at 10:00 (A3).
- **The items suit a car.** A4 scores gata 26/30, the wrap 24 and ponchik 23, with ≤90 s preparation.
- **The economics work for in-house items.** The lavash wrap runs at 29–39% food cost.
- **Penalties:** there is no breakfast-out habit, bought-in pastries run at 45–67% food cost, and the idea is easy to copy.

**Concept 3, broad fast-food (4.6).**
- **The category is saturated and cheap.** KFC (14 units), Tashir (29), Mr. Gyros (17), Karas (10) and 12 shawarma outlets on Glovo; a mainstream meal costs 1,700–3,200 AMD.
- **A4 rejects the core items.** Shawarma scores 17/30 and hot dogs 20/30, both "No".
- **Wendy's is coming** with 20 units planned by 2030.
- **Complex hot production causes long waits**, which is the incumbent's failure mode.
- **Analogs are poor.** McDonald's Bolivia exited over "poor sales and high prices"; McDonald's Kazakhstan exited when imported patties were blocked.

**Concept 4, hybrid roadside convenience (6.8).**
- **It has the widest segment coverage.** Restrooms serve families; walk-up is needed because fewer than half of households have a car; truckers and Georgia traffic stop here.
- **Regional evidence supports forecourt coffee.** WOG averages ≈181 cups per point per day; Dunkin' Georgia has 27 of 72 outlets at fuel stations.
- **Penalties:**
  - Forecourt cafés are already being built: Max Cafe at 10–11 stations, Flash Express Cafe "opening soon" and Shell Café.
  - General retail duplicates 60 fuel stations and 26 convenience shops within 200 m of the M4.
  - EV demand is not evidenced.
  - The partner holds the leverage.

## 6. ATV build from the menu mix (ESTIMATE; mix shares are ASSUMPTIONS)

**Step 1: average price per item.**
- **Handcrafted drink ≈1,320 AMD.** Milk espresso 33% at a weighted 1,385; americano 13% at 1,000; iced latte 17% at 1,600; signature iced 11% at 1,900; jezve 9% at 800; lemonade 9% at 1,100; tea/hot chocolate 8% at 650. Weighted price 1,291, plus modifiers (12% of drinks at +250).
- **Food item ≈970 AMD.** Wrap 25% at 1,500; ponchik 15% at 400; cheese pastry 13% at 700; hats 12% at 900; croissant sandwich 12% at 1,450; gata 10% at 600; lahmajo 8% at 850; cookie/muffin 5% at 600. Weighted price 966.

**Step 2: order types.**

| Order type | Share of orders | Drinks | Food items | Add-ons | Items | Food attach | Order value (AMD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Solo commuter / regional | 60% | 1.05 × 1,320 | 0.35 × 970 | 0.05 × 400 | 1.45 | 35% | 1,745 |
| Group / family leisure | 25% | 2.3 × 1,320 | 1.6 × 970 | 0.4 × 400 | 4.3 | 80% | 4,748 |
| Professional driver | 15% | 1.0 × 950 | 0.6 × 800 | 0.1 × 400 | 1.7 | 55% | 1,470 |
| **Weighted** | 100% | 1.36 | 0.70 | 0.145 | **2.2** | **49%** | **2,455** |

**Step 3: combo discount.**
- 49% of orders contain food, and 40% of those take a combo, so ≈20% of orders get 10% off a 2,290-AMD pair. That is ≈45 AMD per order on average.
- **Base ATV ≈ 2,400 AMD including VAT** (≈2,000 ex-VAT; ≈$6.63).
- Revenue mix: drinks 71%, food 27%, add-ons 2%.

**Cross-checks.**
- The solo order (1,745) matches A4's estimate of 1,540–1,860 and the Coffee Like drive check of ≈1,672 AMD (A2/A5, franchisor claim).
- The base ATV is 69% of the average CBA card ticket (3,473) and below the Numbeo fast-food combo (3,825).

**ATV by season** (group share 18% / 25% / 33%):

| Months | ATV (AMD) |
|---|---|
| Dec–Mar | ≈2,200 |
| Apr–May and Sep–Nov | ≈2,400 |
| Jun–Aug | ≈2,650 |

Weighting these by segment-A monthly traffic (B3) gives ≈2,400 for the year.

**Stress cases.**
- Low: ≈1,950 (winter weekday mix, 25% solo attach, 1,250 average drink).
- High: ≈3,000 (summer weekend, 40% group orders).
- If handcrafted drink prices fall 10%, ATV falls ≈7% to ≈2,230.

**Frequency check.**
- A commuter at 1.5 visits/week and 1,745 AMD spends ≈11.3k AMD/month. That is 4.6% of decile X and 8.2% of decile IX per-capita income (ILCS 2024 incomes, A1 [9]).
- Model repeat frequency at ≤1.5 visits/week.

## 7. Menu architecture

About 30 SKUs at launch, on 2 production lines with a ≤90 s rule.

- **Drinks (10 SKUs):**
  - Jezve-to-go; americano; latte/cappuccino S/M/L; flat white; iced latte.
  - 2 signature iced drinks (apricot-honey, salted caramel).
  - Batch lemonades (sea buckthorn, tarragon, apricot); herbal tea; hot chocolate.
  - Modifiers: oat or lactose-free milk, extra shot, syrup.
- **Hot hand-helds (5–6 SKUs, the hero line):** lavash breakfast wrap; croissant sandwich; zhingyalov hats; folded lahmajo; cheese pastry; optional karkandak as a cheap anchor.
- **Sweet bakery (4 SKUs, bought in):** ponchik filled to order; mini Gavar gata; cookie; muffin.
- **Packaged add-ons:** water, tan, kids' juice, and a gata/ponchik gift box for the return trip and New Year.
- **Combos:** Morning Wrap; Road Snack; Family Road Box (4 hand-helds + 4 drinks, about −10%).
- **Dayparts:**
  - 07–11: commuter breakfast.
  - 11–17: travel and leisure.
  - 17–23: return trips and gifts.
- **Seasonal rotation (3–4 SKUs):** lemonades and iced drinks in summer; herbal tea and punch in winter.
- **Tests only:** 2 energy "Rebel" drinks, one US donut, iced drinks on a cold-brew base.
- **Dropped:** bagels, English-muffin sandwiches, burgers, shawarma, hot dogs, Adjarian khachapuri, fresh juice and fish.

---

## 8. Implications for the design team's decisions (customer lens)

- **CHAMPA as a local brand: keep it.** A US pastiche would be overtaken by Starbucks (via Alshaya) or by Wendy's.
- **2 restrooms and 12 seats: keep them.** Families, leisure trippers and long-distance drivers are the high-basket orders (B3). A walk-up window is mandatory.
- **Two order lanes merging to one pickup lane: supported.** Production capacity is the real bottleneck, because group orders average 4.3 items.
  - Two hot stations plus pre-order are needed to stay under 4 minutes.
  - The US average of ≈245 s is cited by A5 for scale only.
- **EV stalls: keep as an amenity, not a demand driver.** None of the lens files contain EV-fleet data.
- **Long-vehicle bay: keep it**, for truck and marshrutka drivers on foot.
- **Side of the road (right-in/right-out):**
  - The Yerevan-bound side captures weekday morning commuters plus weekend evening leisure returns. The returns are food-led, which suits the hand-helds.
  - The Sevan-bound side captures weekend morning leisure but competes head-on with Coffee House Drive-Thru at km 12.8.
  - A site beyond the km 10–13 cluster, inside segment A (km 9–31, 1.5× seasonality), fits the customer evidence best (ASSUMPTION; for real estate and traffic to confirm).

---

## 9. What would change this verdict (validation before freezing prices)

1. **A price-sensitivity survey** (Van Westendorp; n≥600; Yerevan + Kotayk; quotas by car ownership).
   - If acceptable prices cluster at ≤1,200 for a medium latte, move to a 1,200 M latte. That cuts ATV ≈5–7%.
2. **Intercept surveys and receipt sampling at Coffee House Drive-Thru and Max Cafe km 12.2**, to measure items per car, group share and food attach.
3. **A 2-week pop-up at an M4 fuel station** to test the breakfast wrap and jezve-to-go.
4. **A summer vs February classified traffic count** to settle the leisure share; B3 flags a conflict with B1's segment-B traffic estimate.

## 10. Evidence caveats

- Behavioural data are thin: a 2019 Yerevan survey (n=423) and a 24-hour recall with no stated fieldwork year.
- There are no Armenian surveys on willingness to pay, breakfast-out habits or drive-thru use.
- The Coffee Like figures are a Russian franchisor's "from" claims.
- Glovo prices may sit 0–10% above in-store prices.
- Mix shares, attach rates and group share are labelled ASSUMPTIONS and must be calibrated in the field.

On the M4 Abovyan–Charentsavan segment that needs 1.12% same-side capture, above C6's M4 base of ≈0.63–0.7%. It is easy to permit (≤300 m² category II, no cooks; C5 [7]) and easy to copy.

Sub-scores: Differentiation 7, Defensibility 5, Entry resilience 6, Unit economics/throughput 7, Scalability 7, Regulatory ease 8 (weighted 6.55). This is the only white space that is both open and fast to serve. It loses points on defensibility because FEIN (sandwiches 2,600–3,400; A2 [S25]), Flash Express Cafe and Max Cafe could add hand-helds within 6–12 months (A3 response table, ASSUMPTION), and because Armenian demand for breakfast out is unproven (A3 §3.1).

Co-location also carries a risk that the community classifies the café as part of the station complex: fuel stations are category IV, and EIA Category B applies if fuel storage is ≥5 m³ (C5 [7][26]). lenses.recommended_concept: Concept 2: coffee + hand-held breakfast & bakery (bake-off/assembled, all-electric, no fryers or grills), at affordable-premium prices, under the local CHAMPA identity with American service standards rather than an American identity. Open the first unit on a year-round Yerevan exit corridor (M-5 west inbound or M-2 south edge), not in the M4 km 10–13 cluster. The M4 comes in as unit 2, at the Abovyan–Arzni interchange (B2 cluster C2), once field counts justify it. From Concept 4, borrow only the siting channel and the elements that are cheap or legally required: forecourt pads with CPS or independent CNG operators for lean kiosk units, high-quality accessible restrooms, and EV-ready stalls. Reject convenience retail, any partnership with Max Oil, Flash or Shell (each has its own café brand), and any hot-meal QSR menu.
lenses.positioning_tier: Affordable premium. The core 350 ml cappuccino or latte is priced at AMD 1,400 (≈US$3.87 at 361.93). That is 40% above Coffee House (1,000; A2 [S11]), in line with the Yerevan crowdsourced average (1,342; A2 [S13]) and Cofix in-store (≈1,400, ESTIMATE; A2), 22% below Surf's 300 ml (1,800; A2 [S20]) and 28% below Coffeeshop Company (1,950; A2 [S12]). The entry tier is soorj-to-go at 800 and americano at 1,000, meeting A3's ≤1,200 entry rule. The ceiling is 1,800 for a 470 ml latte and 1,900 for a signature iced drink. Premium pricing is rejected: a 1,950 cappuccino costs ≈1.08 hours of average gross pay (A2 [S1]), 31% of households report running short of money for food (A5 [12]), and the incumbent drive-thru sells at 800–1,200. Mass pricing is rejected too: at ≤1,000 AMD the business would be fighting Coffee House's scale (52 listed branches) and could not recover drive-thru capex at Armenian volumes (C6 §3.9).
key_arguments: Novelty is gone; speed and food are the attack. Coffee House has run an M4 drive-thru (km ≈12.8, Sevan-bound side) since at least Dec 2024 at mass prices: cappuccino 800–1,200, iced drinks ≈900 AMD (A2 [S9][S10]; A3 [21]). It holds 4.9★ on 123 ratings, but its 17 written reviews average 3.76★ and 4 of the 5 written in Jun–Sep 2026 are 1–2★ for 20–60-minute waits and wrong orders (A3 [22]). The incumbent's failure is throughput and accuracy, not demand.

The open white space is coffee plus fast hot breakfast, and it is time-limited. QSR chains list no hot coffee on Glovo, coffee chains sell only sweets and hot dogs, and KFC opens 13 of its 14 restaurants at 10:00 (A3 [1][2]). Concept 2 takes the 07:00–10:00 daypart without entering the meal market where Tashir, Karas, KFC and Wendy's compete.

Concept 3 is strategically dominated. Local anchors are low: Tashir burger 1,300–1,350, Karas shawarma 1,260–1,740, KFC combos 2,800–3,200 AMD (A3 [2][3][4]). Wendy's has a 20-restaurant plan for Armenia by 2030 (A3 [12]) and runs 7 drive-thrus among its 22 mapped Georgian outlets (A5 [32]). A full kitchen pushes service toward the 36–45 cars/h of a single-window lane (C6) and requires certified cooks (C5 [17] Art. 12(6)).

Concept 1 has the weakest unit maths. ATV is ≈2,100 vs ≈2,650 AMD for Concept 2, so breakeven is ≈124 vs ≈98 tx/day (ESTIMATE: scaled from C6's '~100 tx/day near breakeven at 2,600'). On the M4 Abovyan–Charentsavan segment (11,070 same-side light vehicles/day; B4 §3.7) that means 1.12% vs 0.89% capture, both above C6's M4 base of ≈0.63–0.7%. It is also the format Starbucks attacks hardest: 73% of Starbucks company-operated sales are beverages (C6 [7]).

Fuel retail owns the roadside stop and is converging on coffee. Max Oil has ≈11 Max Cafés, including both M4 carriageways at km 12.2, and is still rolling them out. Flash Express Cafe is 'opening soon' and Shell Café is VERIFIED on shell.am (A3 [24][25]; B2). Concept 4's convenience bundle is therefore the majors' home turf. As a channel, though, forecourts work: CPS (53 stations listed, 101 claimed, no food concept) and the independents (36 of 60 M4 stations unbranded) are realistic hosts (A3 [26][23]).

The closest regional analog validates the Concept 2 menu with forecourts as a channel. In Georgia (GDP per capita US$9,692 vs Armenia's US$9,474; A5 [13]), Dunkin' reached 72 mapped outlets. 27 of them (38%) sit within 60 m of a fuel station, mostly Wissol, and only one is tagged as a drive-thru (A5 [32]).

The real moat is the lane system plus land control. Dual order lanes into two windows with runners reach 70–90 cars/h, and a 13-car stack holds the summer-weekend peak of 43–66 cars/h. At 45 arrivals/h a 60 cars/h window needs 10 spaces; a 50 cars/h window needs 28 (C6 §3.4). An incumbent kiosk cannot retrofit this. It needs a new pad, which takes 8–11 months in a settlement or 12–20 months for a greenfield M4 site (C5 §3.10). That gives a lead of roughly 1–1.5 years per site (ESTIMATE).

Starbucks entry argues for a local identity, not an American one. Starbucks held talks in Armenia on 8 Oct 2025 and opened in Georgia in Jul 2026 (REPORTED; A2 [S5][S6][S7]). Its FY2025 10-K dropped the 'particularly drive-thru formats' wording in favour of 'a seat for every occasion' (C6 [7][8]), so entry is likely to be a mall or city-centre coffeehouse (A2 ASSUMPTION). CHAMPA, an Armenian word that already satisfies the Armenian-first signage law (C5 [20][21]), with American service standards is the defensible stance. A5 calls the 'American' brand promise a liability under competition.

Site sequencing follows from exposure. On M-5 Isakov inbound (24,591 same-side light vehicles/day; B4), Concept 2 breaks even at 0.40% capture. C6's urban base of ≈0.71% gives ≈175 tx/day, 1.8× breakeven. On the M4 mid-corridor, C6's base of 0.7% gives ≈77 tx/day, below breakeven. B4 scores the M4 Yerevan edge 3.05 and Hrazdan–Sevan 1.85, against 3.6–4.05 for the urban exits.

Affordable premium is the only tier the evidence supports. A cappuccino at 1,400 costs 0.77 hours of average gross pay (ESTIMATE from A2 [S1]: 1,813 AMD/h). At 1,950 it costs 1.08 hours, against a 1,000-AMD incumbent (A2) and 31% of households short of food money (A5 [12]). A5 recommends 900–1,300 for base coffee and A2 recommends 1,400–1,600 for milk drinks. Our ladder (americano 1,000, latte 1,400) sits where the two meet.

Regulation favours a compact Concept 2 building. A catering building of ≤300 m² is risk category II: a designer's guarantee letter replaces expertise, the planning assignment takes 10 days and the permit 5 (C5 [7]). Keeping impervious paving under 1,000 m² with permeable stalls avoids an EIA Category B process with a council veto (C5 [26]). Forecourt units need a written classification first, because fuel stations are category IV and fuel storage of ≥5 m³ triggers EIA B.

Scalability comes from three formats, all on the same menu: the 171 m² prototype as flagship, a 90–120 m² mid unit, and a 45–65 m² forecourt kiosk built as a relocatable 'non-main structure' (category II, local duty AMD 5–10k × zone coefficient; C5 §3.3). Edge land costs $150–380/m² vs ≈$1,000/m² in the inner city (B4 [16][17]). That supports a pipeline of 4–6 units by 2031 (ASSUMPTION: two parallel site pipelines at 8–20 months each).

Input-cost and FX squeeze. The green-coffee import unit value rose 192% from 2019 to 2025, coffee CPI rose 9.5% in 2025 (A2 [S2][S14]), and food lifts COGS to 31–36% (C6). Affordable-premium pricing leaves little room to pass costs on before reaching the 1,600+ premium-chain tier.

Format precedent. Coffee House has not opened a second drive-thru among its 52 listed branches in about 2 years, which may mean the economics are marginal (A3 ASSUMPTION). 'Drive & Coffee' on the M4's urban section is listed as not operating (B2; Spyur snippet, weak evidence).

Food-compliance friction. Cooks and pastry chefs need vocational credentials (Art. 12(6)), staff medical books must be renewed every 6 months, and from 1 Jan 2027 the HACCP plan becomes a registration document. Sanitary units must connect to a working sewer, which is a problem on non-sewered highway plots (C5 [11][14][16][17]).

# CHAMPA — Competitive strategy, defensibility and scalability: concept verdict

*Lens: competitive strategy, moat and multi-unit roll-out. Date: 2026-10-10. FX: AMD 361.93/USD (CBA, 9 Oct 2026). Status tags follow the research files. Fact-check corrections are applied, for example Cofix's entry date is Jan 2024 (A2 FC #16), Max Cafe has 10 tagged units (≈11 with km 12.2 left; A3 [FC]), and the Starbucks claims are REPORTED, not VERIFIED (A2 FC #18). Citations take the form "file [source no.]".*

---

## 0. Bottom line

| Decision | Call |
|---|---|
| **Concept** | **Concept 2: coffee + hand-held breakfast & bakery (bake-off/assembled), score 6.6/10.** From Concept 4 we borrow only the *siting channel* (CPS or independent CNG forecourts for lean units) and the cheap or legally required elements (quality restrooms, EV-ready stalls). |
| **Ranking** | 2 (6.6) > 4 (5.3) > 1 (3.8) > 3 (2.8) |
| **Tier** | **Affordable premium.** Cappuccino/latte 350 ml **AMD 1,400**; americano 1,000; soorj-to-go 800; iced latte 450 ml 1,600; signature 1,900 |
| **ATV** | **AMD 2,650 base** (≈$7.32) for an urban-edge unit, built from 1.30–1.78 drinks and 0.50–0.80 food items per order. Range 2,200–3,000; M4 leisure-weekend orders ≈3,800 |
| **First site** | Year-round Yerevan exit corridor: M-5 west, inbound side, or the M-2 south edge (B4). **Not** the M4 km 10–13 cluster. The M4 comes in as unit 2, at the Abovyan–Arzni interchange (B2 C2), once field counts justify it |
| **We are not** | "The first American drive-thru on the M4" (false). A burger/shawarma QSR (Wendy's, Tashir and KFC compete there). A convenience store (fuel majors' turf) |

---

## 1. Scoring (0–10)

The weights are an ASSUMPTION reflecting what makes a first-mover position survivable in a small market with a strong local incumbent.

| Criterion (weight) | C1 Specialty beverages | **C2 Coffee + breakfast/bakery** | C3 Broad fast food | C4 Roadside convenience hybrid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Differentiation vs incumbents (20%) | 3 | **7** | 3 | 5 |
| Defensibility / time-to-copy (20%) | 2 | **5** | 2 | 3 |
| Resilience to Starbucks / Wendy's entry (15%) | 2 | **6** | 2 | 6 |
| Unit economics and throughput (15%) | 4 | **7** | 4 | 6 |
| Multi-unit scalability (20%) | 5 | **7** | 2 | 7 |
| Regulatory ease (10%) | 9 | **8** | 5 | 5 |
| **Weighted score** | **3.8** | **6.6** | **2.8** | **5.3** |

**C1, specialty beverages only (3.8).**
- It attacks Coffee House where Coffee House is strongest: 52 listed / 57 claimed branches, a 1,000-AMD latte, app pre-order, an M4 drive-thru, and the FEIN specialty sub-brand with its own Probat roaster (A2 [S8][S9][S11][S26]).
- Fuel cafés already sell espresso on the corridor: Max Coffee and Shell "Signature Espresso" (A3 [24], shell.am).
- Yerevan specialty is an urban sit-down culture of about 16 brands (A2 §3.3).
- ATV ≈2,100 means breakeven ≈124 tx/day (ESTIMATE, scaled from C6's "~100 tx/day near breakeven at 2,600").
- It is the format Starbucks would hit hardest: 73% of Starbucks company-operated sales are beverages (C6 [7]).

**C2, coffee + breakfast/bakery (6.6).**
- It occupies the only gap that is both open and fast to serve:
  - no QSR chain lists hot coffee on Glovo;
  - coffee chains sell sweets and hot dogs;
  - KFC opens 13 of its 14 restaurants at 10:00 (A3 [1][2]).
- Hand-held, bake-off food keeps the window at ≤60 s (C6 §3.5).
- Georgian evidence: Dunkin' (coffee + bakery) scaled to 72 outlets at Armenia's income level (A5 [32]).
- Weaknesses: FEIN, Flash Express Cafe and Max Cafe could copy it within 6–12 months (A3, ASSUMPTION), and Armenian demand for breakfast out is unproven (A3 §3.1).

**C3, broad fast food (2.8).**
- It runs into low anchors: Tashir burger 1,300–1,350, Karas shawarma 1,260–1,740, Mr. Gyros combos 1,736–1,946, KFC combos 2,800–3,200 (A3 [2]–[5]).
- It meets Wendy's on Wendy's home format: 20 units planned by 2030 (A3 [12]), and 7 of its 22 mapped Georgian outlets are drive-thrus (A5 [32]).
- A full kitchen means slower windows (36–45 cars/h for a speaker and one window; C6), certified cooks (C5 [17] Art. 12(6)), and imported-protein supply risk (McDonald's left Kazakhstan over patty supply; A5 [14]).

**C4, convenience hybrid (5.3).**
- It is the best *channel* and a weak *product*.
- In its favour:
  - fuel retail owns the stop (WOG at 117–181 cups per point per day: C6 [28] / A5 [19]; Dunkin' 38% on Georgian forecourts: A5 [32]);
  - existing accesses avoid AMD 27–43M of speed-change lanes (C5 §3.5).
- Against it:
  - convenience retail is the majors' and supermarkets' core business (Max Cafe ≈11, Flash Express, Shell Café, Yerevan City 63, SAS 12; A3);
  - the landowner holds the leverage;
  - restrooms are legally required anyway (C5 [17] Art. 11(4));
  - EV has no evidence base (one charger mapped on the corridor, at km 74; B2);
  - category IV / EIA B classification risk for a café inside a station complex (C5 [7][26]).

**What would change the ranking.**
- If CPS offers turnkey pads with existing access and gives written category II confirmation, C4-as-channel rises to about 6+ and could lead units 2–4.
- If food attach stays below 0.3 after 6 months, fall back to C1-lite kiosks.
- If two-season counts show strong M4 weekend volumes and attach ≥0.8, the M4 moves up to unit 1 or 2.

---

## 3. Defensibility: where the moat is and is not

**No moat:**
- **Concept novelty.** The incumbent drive-thru has operated since at least Dec 2024, so the "first American-style drive-thru on the M4" story does not hold (A2, A3).
- **Price.** Coffee House runs at 1,000 AMD across 52 branches.
- **Recipes and app.** Coffee House already has pre-order.

**Real but time-limited moats:**
1. **Structural throughput.**
   - Dual order lanes into two windows with runners give 70–90 cars/h, against 36–45 for a speaker and one window (C6 §3.4).
   - At 45 arrivals/h, a 60 cars/h window needs 10 stack spaces; a 50 cars/h window needs 28 (C6).
   - The prototype's 13-car stack covers the summer-weekend peak of 43–66 cars/h (C6 §3.4).
   - A kiosk cannot retrofit this. A rival needs a new pad, which takes **8–11 months** in a settlement and **12–20 months** for a greenfield M4 site (C5 §3.10). That is a lead of roughly 1–1.5 years per site (ESTIMATE).
2. **Land control on scarce pads.** Plots with stacking room exist mainly at the city edges ($150–380/m²); inner-city land is ≈$1,000/m² (B4 [16][17]). Securing 2–3 edge pads early is a pre-emption play against Wendy's (A3 §4.6).
3. **Daypart ownership** from 07:00 to 10:00, while KFC opens at 10:00 (A3 [1]).
4. **Local identity.** CHAMPA is an Armenian word and already complies with the Armenian-first signage rule (C5 [20][21]). A5 calls an "American" brand promise a liability under competition.
5. **Hospitality plus speed.** Starbucks' "Back to Starbucks" reset, and Intouch 2026's finding that friendly visits were 25 s faster (C6), favour "Ճամփադ բաց!" service over a sterile speed box.

---

## 4. Entry threats

- **Starbucks.**
  - Likely to come as a coffeehouse-first format in malls or the city centre (A2 ASSUMPTION). Its FY2025 10-K dropped the "drive-thru formats" wording (C6 [7][8]).
  - The overlap is the urban premium beverage occasion (C1), not exit-corridor breakfast-in-the-car (C2).
  - The entry could lift the category's price ceiling (ASSUMPTION), which would help an affordable-premium ladder.
  - Response: do not position as "American"; position as "ours, faster, with food".
- **Wendy's.** The real threat to Concept 3, and a competitor for plots. Stay out of burgers and meals.
- **Fuel majors.** The real threat to Concept 4 and to the highway. Treat forecourts as a *channel* through CPS and independents.

---

| New M4 access (AMD 27–43M lanes, discretionary approval) | Avoid via an interchange site | same | same | Avoided via existing access |

**Implication for the prototype.**

- Interchange or local-road access avoids the decel/accel lanes, worth AMD 27–43M (C5 §4.1).

**Sequencing (ESTIMATE / ASSUMPTION):**
- **Phase 0 (Q4 2026–Q1 2027):**
  - Field counts at the Coffee House M4 drive-thru, which C6 calls "the single most decisive calibration point", and at 2–3 candidate sites.

**Reading the build.**
- Food share is 27–31%, conservative against C6's 30–45% range for an Armenian coffee-and-food unit.
- Regional cross-check: the beverage-only spend of 1,820 per order is 9% above Coffee Like's Russian car-pavilion check of ≈1,670 AMD (A2 [S24]).
- Revenue at 120 tx/day × 2,650 × 360 days ≈ AMD 114.5M (≈$316k).

**Comparator ATVs (ESTIMATE).**

---

## 9. Key risks

1. Coffee House fixes its operations or opens a second drive-thru within months.
2. Fuel majors add hot hand-helds within 6–12 months.
3. Starbucks enters within 12–36 months.
4. Wendy's competes for the same edge pads.
5. Breakfast attach comes in below 0.35.
6. Window time drifts above 70 s, and the stack needed jumps from 10 to 28 cars.
7. Forecourt classification (category IV / EIA B), an EIA council veto, or discretionary M4 access approval.
8. Partner hold-up on forecourt leases.
9. No M4 traffic count since 2008, and model capture of ≈2.4% vs a benchmark of ≈0.6–0.8%.
10. COGS squeeze from coffee costs (+192% unit value 2019–25; coffee CPI +9.5% in 2025).
11. Coffee House has not opened a second drive-thru; "Drive & Coffee" is listed as closed (weak evidence).
12. Food-compliance friction: cooks' credentials, medical books, HACCP plan at registration from 2027.

---

## 10. Challenges to the design-team givens

- **M4 as first site:** challenged. Use the urban exit corridor first (B4 scores 3.6–4.05 vs 3.05 for the M4 Yerevan edge and 1.85 for Hrazdan–Sevan).
- **"American-style":** keep the service standards, drop the identity.
- **CHAMPA:** keep it. It is local, compliant with the language law, and defensive against Starbucks.
- **171 m² prototype:** right as the flagship, but the roll-out unit is 90–120 m² plus a kiosk.
- **Restrooms:** keep. They are legally required, so make cleanliness a brand promise for leisure stops.
- **2 EV stalls:** build them EV-ready, with partner-funded chargers. EV is not a pillar.
- **Decel/accel lanes:** avoid them by choosing interchange or local-road access.

challenge.verdict:
The menu and the price tier hold up, but the recommendation is not investable as framed. I read all six files in full: A2, A3, A4, A5, C2 and C6.

What holds:
- **Concept 2's menu.** Coffee plus a narrow set of Armenian hand-held items, bake-off or assembled, with no fryer, grill or cook.
- **Affordable-premium positioning.**
- **Rejecting Concept 3, the American identity, EV charging, convenience retail and the 171 m² prototype as unit 1.**

What fails:
- **Unit 1 does not return capital.** The lenses still ask an investor to commit AMD 110–150M to it. Lens 1's own table shows the best case (Concept 4, co-located) losing AMD 8.2M a year at the C6 base of about 110 tx/day. At 150 tx/day it earns +8.7M a year, a simple payback of about 12.6 years (ESTIMATE: 110 / 8.7).
- **The lenses contradict each other on ticket and break-even.** Average ticket is 2,050, 2,400 or 2,650 depending on the lens. Break-even is 98 or 129–176 tx/day. All of these sit above the Armenian and regional anchors:
  - A2: 1,300–1,500 AMD of drinks per order, "not 1,800+".
  - A4: about 1,540–1,860 AMD per order including food.
  - Coffee Like: about 1,672 AMD per check.

**1. Is the price realistic against Coffee House (about 1,000 AMD)?** Only as a ceiling, and only with an entry tier.
- 1,400 AMD for a 350 ml latte is supportable: 40% above Coffee House on Glovo, and about the Numbeo average of 1,342.
- Lens 1's 1,600 latte (400 ml) and 1,700 iced latte are not. Lens 2/3's 1,600 iced latte is still 60–78% above the 900–1,000 iced drinks at the Coffee House drive-thru 1 km away (A2 fact-check).
- For a Kotayk earner the 1,400 latte costs about 1.17 hours of gross pay. That is roughly what a 1,950 AMD Coffeeshop Company cappuccino costs at the national average wage.
- No Armenian willingness-to-pay data exists.

**2. Does food add margin or only complexity?** It adds thin margin and real differentiation.
- Using C2's own wrap cost (628 AMD, not A4's 457), the food mix runs at about 43–44% COGS, not 37%.
- Food covers its own extra fixed cost only above about 26–37% attach (ESTIMATE). That is the middle of A4's attach range, which is itself an unvalidated assumption. Glovo shows no breakfast-out habit (1 of 33 food stores under "Breakfast").
- Keep food, but justify it as a traffic driver and a differentiator, not as a margin engine.

**3. Does the hybrid format dilute the brand or win on restrooms and EV?** It wins as a channel and loses as a product.
- Regional coffee scaled on fuel forecourts: Dunkin' in Georgia (27 of 72 outlets), WOG in Ukraine (117–181 cups per point per day).
- EV demand has zero evidence in these files.
- Convenience retail duplicates 60 fuel stations and 26 convenience shops already on the M4.
- Partner rent or revenue-share terms are unknown. Max Oil, Flash and Shell each already run their own café.

**4. Is "American-style" a selling point?** No. As an identity it is a liability: Starbucks failed in Israel and Australia, Dunkin' left Poland, Wendy's plans 20 Armenian units, and Starbucks-Alshaya is circling. As a service standard (speed) it is copyable within months, and it is worth less in low-congestion Yerevan.

**5. What would a disciplined investor choose for unit 1?**
- **Menu:** Concept 2-lite. One in-house wrap plus 3–5 bake-off or bought-in items, all-day, assembled centrally in Yerevan.
- **Prices:** M latte 1,400, iced latte 1,400–1,500, americano 1,000, jezve 800, ponchik 400.
- **Format:** a relocatable 45–65 m² kiosk with one lane, a tablet runner and a walk-up window.
- **Site:** a CPS or independent CNG forecourt, or an urban-edge exit site with existing access. Not the M4 km 10–13 cluster, and not a greenfield pad on a 90 km/h road.
- **Leave out:** own seats, own restrooms, EV charging and retail.
- **Capex ceiling:** about AMD 35M bottom-up, at most about 80M (ESTIMATE; derivation in problem 1).
- **Before any capex, pass a Phase-0 gate:**
  - summer and winter counts at the Coffee House M4 drive-thru;
  - intercept surveys and receipt sampling at Coffee House and Max Cafe;
  - a Van Westendorp price survey, n ≥ 600, including Kotayk;
  - a 2-week forecourt pop-up.
- **Later units:** a permanent mid unit only after a site proves about 190–220 tx/day. The prototype needs about 390 tx/day for a 5-year payback (lens 1), so it is not an investable unit-1 or unit-2 format.
